clue.text: Judas returned bread — deceit!

indicators.note: something returned comes back the way it went, so the letters are read from the far end

blocks.note: roti is an Indian flatbread
art in the sense of cunning or trickery

explanation.surface: Judas, at the Last Supper, hands back the bread while hiding his treachery.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are joined first and then the whole string is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name stands for any betrayer.

clue.text: Birdbrained fellow getting close to warbler?

definitions.text: Birdbrained fellow getting close to warbler?

blocks.note: a twit is a foolish person
Cher, the pop singer, is a warbler

explanation.surface: A dim enthusiast creeps up on a small songbird.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes an obsessive birdwatcher sneaking up to see a warbler; 'getting close to' simply means the second piece goes next to the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitcher is a British term for a keen birdwatcher who travels to see rare species.

clue.text: Naked vicars causing offence

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters are removed

blocks.note: parsons are vicars

explanation.surface: Clergymen stripping off would scandalise their congregations.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: No-one's coming up after 10, creating unease

indicators.note: in a down answer, coming up means read from the bottom upwards
after means these letters follow the number in the grid

blocks.note: the number written out
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Nobody turning up after ten o'clock makes the host anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No-one's' is split into its parts: no, one as a numeral, and the s.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is mental strain or nervousness, which is a state of unease.

clue.text: Grant carries about picture

indicators.note: carries suggests the first word holds the second up front, so it comes first

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
to grant is to present, give formally

explanation.surface: A person named Grant carries something around, like a portrait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a name but is a verb; the joining word is loose, so read it as the gift taking about along at its front.
explanation.definitionFit: To represent can mean to depict, as a painting pictures its subject.

clue.text: Uncapped men given limitless opportunities to improve

indicators.note: without a cap means the head of the word is taken off
with no limits means both boundary letters of the word are dropped

blocks.note: men without its first letter
chances with its first and last letters removed

explanation.surface: A sports selector gives untried players plenty of chances to get better.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncapped men' reads as players not yet picked for their country, but it means only the word men loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance something is to raise its quality, a close synonym of improve.

clue.text: It's topless juggling? Correct

indicators.note: in a down answer, losing the top means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: 'it' is old slang for sex or sex appeal
juggling is an example of a stage act

explanation.surface: Someone asks if juggling without a shirt is the right answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as a word for sex is a crossword convention from early twentieth-century slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and correct both mean accurate, without error.

clue.text: Buzz preceding rap routine

indicators.note: preceding means this piece comes first, above the next one in a down answer

blocks.note: a hum is a buzzing sound
to rap is to drum with the fingers

explanation.surface: A droning sound comes before a set rap performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rap' suggests music, but it is a tapping verb; 'routine' is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Humdrum means dull and ordinary, close to routine in the sense of monotonous.

clue.text: The sound of dub beat in disco

indicators.note: the sound of tells us we want a word pronounced like the one indicated, not spelt like it

blocks.note: to dub is to make someone a knight
to beat is to club

explanation.surface: Dub music's pounding rhythm is heard in a dance hall.
explanation.walkthrough: Dub is a reggae style, but here it means knighting with a sword; only the first piece is spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a nightclub where people dance to recorded music.

clue.text: Half of Neanderthals fighting for a set of nine things

indicators.note: half of means only the first six of the twelve letters are kept
fighting suggests things thrown about in a scuffle, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Cavemen brawl over a group of nine objects.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennead comes from the Greek for nine and means a group of nine, such as the nine Egyptian gods of Heliopolis.

clue.text: Uncomfortable condition initially endured by northern playwright

indicators.note: initially points to only the opening letter of the following word

blocks.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome
first letter of endured
N is the standard abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A northern playwright suffers some awkward ailment that he has had to put up with.
explanation.walkthrough: IBS is a common abbreviation for irritable bowel syndrome; 'northern' looks like it describes the playwright, who was indeed Norwegian, but it gives a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Bird with one leg finally caught in reconfigured mantrap

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it
something reconfigured has had its parts set out in a new arrangement
something caught in a trap ends up enclosed within it

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Roman numeral for one
last letter of leg

explanation.surface: A bird with one leg has got the other caught in a cruel trap set for poachers.
explanation.walkthrough: A mantrap was a large steel trap for catching trespassers; its letters are rearranged and the two single letters sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions that turns white in winter.

clue.text: New badly-lit hospital department east of Co. Mayo?

definitions.note: the question mark flags mayonnaise as an example

indicators.note: in an across answer, east of means placed to the right of, so these pieces follow

blocks.note: taken as written; Co. is short for county
N is the abbreviation for new
a badly lit room is dim
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department

explanation.surface: A new, gloomy hospital wing sits on the eastern side of County Mayo in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Co. Mayo' reads as the Irish county, but Co. is wordplay and Mayo is short for mayonnaise, which is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a sauce served alongside food, an example of a condiment.

clue.text: Carriage drawn by horse or rodent? That's funny

blocks.note: a rat is a rodent
a laugh at something funny

explanation.surface: Someone imagines a carriage pulled by a rat instead of a horse and finds it comic.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is rare: it comes from Sanskrit and is used in India.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratha is an Indian chariot or carriage, traditionally pulled by horses or oxen.

clue.text: Relatives of former partner looked after smart Parisian friend inside

indicators.note: inside means the French word sits within the word for smart

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
to tend is to look after
fly is slang for sharp or smart
ami is French for friend

explanation.surface: The family of an ex-partner cared for a stylish French friend staying with them.
explanation.walkthrough: Fly, meaning knowing or sharp, is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended family includes aunts, uncles, cousins and grandparents beyond the household, all of them relatives.

clue.text: Large present's top tearing the tight wrapping paper

indicators.note: in a down answer, the top of a word is its first letter
tearing rips the wrapping apart, so all these letters are scattered and rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of present
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rips the snug wrapping paper off a big gift.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: 'tight wrapping' only colours the surface, since the jumbled letters need no container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Telegraph is a British daily newspaper, so it is a paper.

clue.text: Those eating ordered a string of sausages?

blocks.note: first meaning: the ranking of creatures by what eats what
second meaning, cryptic: linked sausages are literally a chain of something to eat

explanation.walkthrough: The first part reads like diners placing an order, but it means eaters arranged in sequence; the question mark flags the playful second meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: In ecology it is the sequence of organisms each eating the one below, and a string of sausages is edible links.

clue.text: One is overwhelmed by convulsion, and hot — terrible flu? Spot on

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means swamped, so the first word sits inside the second
terrible suggests something in a bad state, so the letters are mixed up

blocks.note: a fit is a convulsion
a, the indefinite article, means one
H for hot, as on a tap
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A patient seized by shaking and fever has a bad dose of flu, the diagnosis being right.
explanation.definitionFit: Faithful can mean accurate or true to the original, as a faithful copy is spot on.

clue.text: One who has this is liable to experience unconfined joy

definitions.text: One who has this is liable to experience unconfined joy

blocks.note: surface reading: the phrase means unrestrained delight, as if this condition brought happiness

blocks.clueFragment: One who has this is liable to experience unconfined joy
blocks.note: setter's reading: a sufferer from this fear is happy only when not shut in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Unconfined joy' is a stock phrase for wild celebration, but here it means joy at not being confined.
explanation.definitionFit: This phobia is an irrational fear of enclosed spaces, so freedom from confinement brings relief.

clue.text: Virtuous puritan housed in ramshackle hut

indicators.note: housed in means lodged within, so one word sits inside the other
ramshackle means tumbledown, so the letters of the dwelling are knocked into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a prig is a smugly moralistic person

explanation.surface: A strait-laced, moral person lives in a run-down shack.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright means honest and morally principled, the same as virtuous.

clue.text: Hotel shoddily built by a slippery character from school

indicators.note: shoddily built means put together badly, so the letters are in the wrong order

blocks.note: Hotel is the radio code word for H
built plus a, taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dodgy pupil from the local school put up a jerry-built hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' suggests pupils, but it is a school of fish; 'slippery character' is a fish, not a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: The halibut is a large flatfish, slippery to hold, and fish swim in schools.

clue.text: Line through father, son and mother — it's in the blood

indicators.note: a line drawn through something runs inside it, so the letter goes within

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
L is the abbreviation for line
S is the abbreviation for son
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A family line passing from father through son and mother is hereditary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's in the blood' sounds like a family trait, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Plasma is the pale liquid part of blood in which the cells are suspended.

clue.text: Knock back magnificent beer

indicators.note: knock back suggests sending backwards, so the word is read from the end

blocks.note: regal means royal, magnificent

explanation.surface: An instruction to down a wonderful beer in one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock back' is slang for drinking quickly, which fits the beer, but here it reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Lager is a light, bottom-fermented type of beer.

clue.text: Brilliant programme on before Easter?

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed directly ahead of what follows

blocks.note: Excel is Microsoft's spreadsheet program
Lent is the forty days of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A viewer is delighted that a show is scheduled ahead of the Easter holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Programme' suggests television but means software here.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent and brilliant are both strong words of praise meaning outstandingly good.

clue.text: Losing head, sexist angrily leaves

indicators.note: losing its head means the word loses its first letter
acting angrily means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Losing his temper, a sexist storms out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' is a verb, not foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: Exits is the verb meaning goes out of or departs, the same as leaves.

clue.text: Some commoner I call 'Heather'

indicators.note: some means only a portion of the following words is taken

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word into the next two

explanation.surface: A person of humble birth names someone Heather.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes make Heather look like a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers.

clue.text: Exotic grail's broken by Chinese people in Himalayan valley

indicators.note: exotic means strange and foreign, so these letters take an unfamiliar order
a word broken by another is split open with the other placed in the gap

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the Han are China's majority ethnic group

explanation.surface: An exotic holy grail is smashed by Chinese people somewhere in the Himalayas.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the fictional paradise valley of James Hilton's novel Lost Horizon, set in the Himalayan mountains.

clue.text: Digest soft cheese loudly

blocks.note: brie is a soft French cheese
f stands for forte, the musical instruction to play loudly

explanation.surface: Someone eats a soft cheese and their stomach rumbles noisily as it is processed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digest' looks like a verb about the cheese, but it is a noun meaning summary; 'loudly' is not a sound cue but the musical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary, and a brief is a short summary of facts.

clue.text: A cheat's reformed to become a loyal companion

indicators.note: reformed means formed again in a different shape, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheat mends his ways and becomes a trustworthy friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is from Virgil's Aeneid, where Achates is the hero's constant friend, often called fidus Achates.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates was the faithful friend of Aeneas, so his name is used for any loyal companion.

clue.text: Final party game

blocks.note: net as in final, after all deductions
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: The deciding party game of the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Final' reads as the last event, but it means net, as in a net figure after deductions.
explanation.definitionFit: Netball is a team sport, popular in British schools, in which players score by throwing a ball through a high hoop.
